title: Incremental SLI Replay Store and Insight Probes for Console Analytics
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: Investigations for tenant SLI regressions require re-running large slices of pipeline data or relying on coarse aggregated metrics. This slows incident resolution, causes noisy pager churn, and prevents engineers/PMs from quickly validating fixes.

Goal: Build an incremental, queryable snapshot store of SLI-relevant events (prefixes, trace references, metric deltas) that supports fast 'replay' queries for a bounded time window and enables journey-linked heatmap visualizations in the Console. The store should be cost-conscious (compactified snapshots), support TTL-based retention, and be usable by on-call, SRE, and product teams for debugging and quality verification.

Scope: Backend service + ETL to produce compact snapshots per request journey; query API for the Console dashboard; migration strategy for backfilled historical data (best-effort for 30 days); integration with existing tracing and SLO systems for correlation. Excludes UI polish of dashboard widgets beyond MVP visualizations.
acceptance_criteria: A compact snapshot format is defined and documented with field-level schema and size budget (<= 4KB per snapshot typical).
ETL job reliably writes incremental snapshots for 95% of incoming analytic events during peak traffic in staging.
Query API can return journey-linked SLI snapshots for a given tenant+route+time-range in <300ms median for 90th percentile queries in staging.
Console dashboard can render a heatmap of per-journey latency buckets using snapshot data (MVP: 5 minute granularity).
Runbook updated with steps to use snapshots for SLI regression triage and fallbacks if store is unavailable.
design_notes: Snapshot contents: request metadata (tenant, route, model_id, seq_len), sampled prefix hashes, KV-cache hits, trace_id, short tokenized length histogram, and delta metrics (latency_ms, cpu_ms, gpu_ms). Keep PII out of snapshots.
Storage choice: RocksDB-backed micro-shards per-tenant for low read latency with an S3 cold tier for older segments. Shard keys: tenant_id::date::route_hash.
Write pattern: streaming compaction from analytics pipeline with idempotent upserts; low-overhead sampling weight tuned per tenant class to cap storage.
Indexing: maintain per-tenant Bloom filters for quick existence checks; precompute 1-minute aggregates to speed heatmap rendering.
Correlation: link snapshots to existing traces via trace_id; if trace not available, include top-3 inferred call-signatures.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary, week 1): write-only to store for <5% traffic from internal dev tenants; monitor write success rate and cost.
Phase 2 (expanded sampling, week 2): increase sampling to 20% for staging tenants and enable query API for SRE tools.
Phase 3 (production gated, week 3): enable read for Console beta users and ramp writes to target sampling configured per customer class.
Rollback: disable ETL writes and fall back to aggregated metrics if any storage pressure or latency regressions occur.
migration_plan: Backfill: best-effort ingest of last 30 days using parallelized batch job that compacts historical events into snapshot format. Priority: top 50 high-usage tenants.
Schema evolution: add version field to snapshots and maintain compatibility layer in query API to handle v1 -> v2 migrations.
Cost estimate: initial backfill expected to read 3TB and write ~150GB of compact snapshots for 30-day window (approx).
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Storage cost growth if sampling not tuned. Mitigation: enforce per-tenant budget and automated downsampling when budget exceeded.
Risk: Snapshot format leaks sensitive tokens. Mitigation: enforce redaction layer and schema validation in ETL; security review before prod rollout.
Risk: Query latency spikes under bursty dashboard use. Mitigation: serve hot 1-minute aggregates and apply per-tenant rate limits on ad-hoc replay queries.
test_plan: Unit tests for snapshot encoder/decoder and schema validators.
Integration tests exercising end-to-end write->query path against staging shards.
Load test: simulate 2x peak ingest with synthetic traces and validate <1% write error rate and query p95 <500ms.
Chaos test: simulate shard failures and validate read fallbacks to cold tier and correct error returns to Console.
